title: Fluorine Fails, Oxygen Wins: Highest Oxidation States in Oxides and Fluorides
subject: Chemistry
objective: A metal reaches its highest oxidation state only with oxygen or fluorine. Fluorine is the more electronegative, yet manganese's highest fluoride is MnF₄ (+4) while its oxide reaches +7 (Mn₂O₇, MnO₄⁻): one oxygen forms a multiple bond and counts two electrons, one fluorine counts only one. From Sc₂O₃ to Mn₂O₇ the highest oxide's oxidation state equals the group number.

fill.q: The highest oxidation state of Mn in a fluoride is +____.
In MnO₄⁻ the oxidation state of Mn is +____.
Oxygen stabilises high oxidation states because it forms ____ bonds with metals.
In the highest oxides from Sc to Mn, the oxidation state equals the ____ number.

tf.explain: Fluorine is more electronegative; oxygen wins by multiple bonding.

ar.r: Oxygen can form multiple bonds with metals.
